conventions.frame: metres, glTF Y-up, forward +Z, vehicle right = -X, origin on the ground at the footprint centre
conventions.hierarchy: Transform nodes from the spec (root, hull, turret, gun_pivot, wheel_*, roadwheel_*, sprocket_*, idler_*) are EMPTIES; their geometry is a child mesh named <node>_geo with a sibling <node>_geo_LOD1. This keeps every mesh a leaf so LOD switching by toggling mesh.visible (as soldier.js does) never hides child transforms. track_L/track_R are leaf meshes directly under hull (with track_L_LOD1/track_R_LOD1).
conventions.pivots: turret yaws about local Y at the ring centre; gun_pivot pitches about local X at the trunnion; wheels/roadwheels/sprockets/idlers spin about local X at the hub
conventions.running_gear_parent: wheels, sprockets, idlers and tracks are children of hull (not root) so hiding hull for the wreck swap hides the whole intact vehicle
conventions.hidden_by_default: nodes with extras.hidden = true (three.js userData.hidden): every *_LOD1 and hull_wreck / turret_wreck. The game must set visible=false on load (glTF has no visibility flag).
conventions.wrecks: hull_wreck and turret_wreck are direct children of root (siblings of hull) so the turret wreck can be thrown independently; turret_wreck origin = turret ring centre. BTR wreck sits on bare rims (tyres burnt away, hull dropped ~0.3 m); tank wreck sits 4 cm lower. Wrecks use decimated (~45%) copies of the LOD0 geometry with a burnt material sharing the paint atlas UVs.
conventions.lod: <mesh>_LOD1 = collapse-decimated copy (~30% tris) in the same local space as <mesh>; instanced wheel meshes share one LOD1 mesh.
conventions.materials: <vehicle>_paint: one 2048 atlas (albedo JPEG 2048, ORM PNG 1024 [R=1, G=roughness, B=metalness], normal PNG 1024) for all painted steel, rubber tyres, wood, canvas, MG metal; glass; light_lens; track (alphaMode MASK) ; <vehicle>_wreck + track_wreck for the burnt variants.
conventions.track_uv: track_L/track_R: U = link index along the loop (1.0 per link, 97 links -> U 0..97), V across the profile. Scroll the track material map/normalMap/roughnessMap offset.x by distance_travelled / track_link_pitch_m (sign by direction; L and R share the material, so clone it per side for skid steering). Guide horns and the gaps between links are alpha-tested, so they scroll with the texture.
conventions.cope_cage: t72b3 only: separate mesh node turret/cope_cage (+LOD1) so the game can toggle it.
conventions.empties: muzzle, coax_muzzle under gun_pivot; smoke_launchers and (tanks) commander_hatch under turret; exhaust, dismount_L, dismount_R and (BTR) commander_hatch under hull. Tank dismount_L/R mark crew bail-out points beside the hull.
conventions.ride_seats: Desant riding positions: empties ride_seat_1..N under hull (BTR: 8, T-72: 6), listed per vehicle in ride_seats. Origin = point under the rider pelvis on the sitting surface; local +Z = direction the rider faces, +Y = up. extras.seat_type: "edge" = sitting on a deck edge / fender bin with the legs hanging over the side (thighs along +Z, knees ~0.44 m out, shins down; on the BTR the upper hull side below the roof edge slopes outward ~39 deg, so angle the shins out ~30 deg) or "deck" = sitting on the deck, legs forward along +Z (knees up). Seats parent to hull, so riders follow hull motion; turret traverse never reaches them (ride_clearance.turret_sweep_radius_m vs min_rider_margin_m, cope cage included), but the gun barrel does: ride_clearance.gun_min_elevation_to_clear_riders_deg is the elevation the gun needs before it may traverse over riders; when gun_can_clear_riders is false (T-72) lock the turret to the forward arc while riders are aboard. The rider proxy used for these checks is drawn by tools/blender/vehicles/preview.html?seats=1.
